title: Embedded interfaces, type assertion and `type switch`

videos.script: Lesson 28 put values into an any and paid for it. This lesson is about getting them back out without a crash. First, a smaller step. An interface can be built out of other interfaces. io.ReadWriter is io.Reader and io.Writer, written as two lines. {{embedded}} Then the type assertion, in its second form. It answers with a value and a yes or no, instead of a panic. Pointed at an interface, it asks a value what else it can do. The standard library does that inside io.Copy. {{assertion}} Last, the type switch. One switch walks a JSON document of unknown shape, a case for each type the decoder can produce. And fmt uses one to decide whether your type gets its Error or its String method. {{switch}} By the end you can read any value safely, whatever type it turns out to hold.
